questions.prompt: Which timing procedure gives a trustworthy single-launch latency?
options: Warm up, then repeat (synchronise, read clock) many times and take the median
Average of all runs including the first
questions.explanation: Warm-up, synchronisation and a robust statistic.

questions.prompt: Back to back, 1,000 launches of a 2 µs kernel with 4 µs launch overhead take how long in total, in µs?
questions.explanation: Launch-bound: one launch per 4 µs (plus a final 2 µs).

questions.prompt: SOL: DRAM 22%, L2 17%, issue 97%, FMA share 3%, lots of atomic serialisation. Diagnosis and first fix?
options: Issue-bound on contended atomics: privatise (registers or shared memory), then merge
questions.explanation: Serialised atomics are issued instructions that do no useful work.

questions.prompt: A kernel is DRAM-bound at 98% SOL but reads one float of every 32-byte struct. What can the kernel itself do?
options: Very little: the waste is in the data layout. Change it upstream (structure of arrays) or fuse the consumer
questions.explanation: At the roof, only fewer bytes help, and here that means a different layout.

questions.prompt: 48 equal tiles on 16 SMs, one at a time per SM: tail efficiency, in %?
49 equal tiles on 16 SMs, one at a time per SM: tail efficiency, in %?
questions.explanation: 4 waves, 64 slots: 49/64. One extra tile costs a whole wave.

questions.prompt: What does a pointer chase isolate?
options: Latency: each load depends on the previous one

questions.prompt: In a microbenchmark sweep, the time per byte jumps at some size. Before calling it a cache capacity, what should you rule out?
options: A change of regime unrelated to caches, e.g. latency-limited at small sizes, bandwidth-limited at large ones
questions.explanation: Design experiments so that only the target property changes.

questions.prompt: Stream-K vs split-K: what's the key difference?
options: Split-K splits every tile's k-loop by a fixed factor; Stream-K gives each persistent block an equal range of iterations across tiles
questions.explanation: Stream-K balances total work exactly; split-K just makes more pieces.

questions.prompt: A PR makes a kernel 3× slower; coalescing dropped from 0.86 to 0.25 and sectors per request rose from 4.7 to 16. Most likely cause?
options: Each thread now handles consecutive elements, so a warp's lanes access addresses far apart
questions.explanation: Coarsen across the grid (stride by the thread count), not within a thread's own contiguous chunk.
